topStories.headline: Cow Hollow Victorian Sells for $8.6M — Nearly $3 Million Over Asking in Two Weeks
topStories.dek: A 1911 Thomas Patterson Ross-designed home on Filbert Street closed at 46 percent above its list price, the latest sign of fierce competition for scarce luxury homes in these neighborhoods.
topStories.body:
The Cow Hollow luxury market delivered another eye-catching result last week. The three-story, 4,190-square-foot home at 2441 Filbert Street hit the market September 18 at $5.9 million and sold two weeks later, on October 2, for $8.6 million — a gap of $2.7 million, or roughly 46 percent above asking. The sale was reported by The Real Deal and the San Francisco Business Times on October 8.

The home, designed in 1911 by noted San Francisco architect Thomas Patterson Ross for the Lehmann family, sits on an unusually deep lot and includes a separate cottage in the rear garden. Views of the Golden Gate Bridge, the Palace of Fine Arts, and San Francisco Bay are visible from the top floor. The listing was handled by Nina Hatvany of Compass.

The transaction is the most recent in a string of dramatic overbids in the area. According to Compass data cited by the Business Times, 73 percent of offers in San Francisco for homes listed above $4 million were all-cash last month, a figure that agents say reflects the outsized purchasing power flowing into the city from the technology sector.

The Filbert Street sale also echoes the broader Cow Hollow trend: the 12-month rolling median house price in the neighborhood through early 2026 stood at $6.45 million, according to Compass market data — already among the highest residential medians in the country. With inventory remaining thin, real estate observers expect competitive bidding to continue through the fall.

topStories.headline: Marina Safeway Lawsuit: Federal Case Moves Forward as City Prepares Response
topStories.dek: The federal suit challenging the fast-tracked approval of an 848-unit twin-tower project at 15 Marina Blvd. remains active, with the city and developer both signaling they will contest it in court.
topStories.body:
The federal lawsuit filed in September over the proposed Marina Safeway redevelopment continues to move through the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California. The suit was filed by the YesAND Foundation, Neighborhoods United San Francisco, and four Marina District residents, and names the city of San Francisco, its Planning and Public Health departments, PG&E, developer Align Real Estate Partners, and Safeway parent company Albertsons as defendants.

At the heart of the complaint is the allegation that city planners improperly granted streamlined approval under Assembly Bill 2011 — a state housing law designed to accelerate housing production — for a 2.6-acre site that the suit says is contaminated and therefore ineligible for that fast-track process. The proposal calls for a 22-story and an 18-story tower containing 848 apartments at 15 Marina Boulevard. Plaintiffs are asking the court to halt the project until full environmental reviews are completed.

A spokesperson for the City Attorney's office said the city will review the complaint and respond in court after being formally served. Developer Align Real Estate Partners has maintained that the project fully complies with state law. District 2 Supervisor Stephen Sherrill has previously opposed the project over its scale and the unresolved contamination questions, though San Francisco planning officials determined in August that the project meets AB 2011's eligibility requirements.

The lawsuit is being watched as a potential test case for AB 2011 itself. Attorneys for the plaintiffs have argued that the state streamlining law was not designed to bypass toxic-site safeguards, while the developer contends it has met all applicable environmental investigation requirements. No hearing date has been publicly announced.

topStories.headline: West Harbor Dredge Due This Month as Marina Yacht Harbor Eyes Fall Sand Buildup
topStories.dek: SF Rec & Park's October 1 update shows the channel open but a second dredge episode imminent, following a spring effort that removed nearly 39,000 cubic yards of sediment after a months-long blockage drew city-wide attention.
topStories.body:
San Francisco's Marina Yacht Harbor is navigating its second sedimentation episode of 2026. The SF Recreation and Parks Department's October 1 weekly update lists the West Harbor channel as open — but cautioned mariners to navigate with care — and notes that a fall dredging round is still on the calendar. According to the SF Marina Harbor Association, the spring episode was completed on June 28 and was always intended to be followed by another dredge in October.

The spring work, conducted by Dutra Group, removed 38,710 cubic yards of sediment from the entrance channel and restored navigable depth after months of disruption that drew widespread attention in May. That buildup had shallowed and narrowed the West Harbor entrance to the point where rescue watercraft could not exit during at least one emergency call off Crissy Field — a gap in public safety that city officials later acknowledged.

A U.S. Coast Guard Local Notice to Mariners issued in September confirmed that Marinship Development has dredging operations permitted for the San Francisco Marina West Basin through November 30, 2026. Channel width as of October 1 measured approximately 75 feet at a tide height of 3.1 feet.

Longer term, the city is designing a new West Harbor breakwater it says could reduce dredging frequency by 10 to 15 years once constructed. That project is currently in the environmental review and detailed design phase, with construction of the breakwater targeted for 2027.

events.title: Fleet Week Air Show — Blue Angels over San Francisco Bay
events.location: Marina Green, 200 Marina Blvd, Marina District
events.description: The U.S. Navy Blue Angels headline three days of aerial performances over the Bay between the Golden Gate Bridge and Alcatraz. The show also features the F-22 Raptor Demo Team, the USMC F-35B Demo Team, and a United Airlines 777 demonstration. The Parade of Ships runs Friday morning, Oct. 9, from 11 a.m. to noon past Marina Green. Free from public areas; premium seating ticketed.

moreNews.headline: Supervisor Sherrill Faces November General Election for District 2 Seat
moreNews.body: District 2 Supervisor Stephen Sherrill, who represents the Marina, Cow Hollow, Pacific Heights, and Presidio Heights, won the June 2 special primary election with approximately 70 percent of the vote, defeating neighborhood activist Lori Brooke. However, because he was originally appointed rather than elected, his seat is again on the ballot in the November 3, 2026 general election. Sherrill was appointed in December 2024 by then-Mayor London Breed after Catherine Stefani was elected to the California State Assembly. He has been a consistent supporter of Mayor Daniel Lurie's housing agenda, including the Family Zoning Plan, and has opposed the Marina Safeway project on environmental and scale grounds.
